source_title: Chuck Lorre's charity breaks ground on final building, serves 1.5m meals
source_excerpt: A major expansion of a Los Angeles charity backed by The Big Bang Theory creator Chuck Lorre reached another milestone on October 29, 2026, when Project Angel Food broke ground on the final building of its new campus. The organisation, which prepares and delivers medically tailored meals to people living with serious illnesses, is developing the two-building facility with support from The Chuck Lorre Family Foundation. According to Project Angel Foodâs official announcement, the new Community Outreach Center will bring client services, nutrition education, volunteer facilities and research programmes together at its Hollywood site. The development follows the opening of the campus kitchen in February.Final building begins construction at Hollywood campusThe groundbreaking ceremony marked the start of the second and final phase of The Chuck Lorre Family Foundation Kitchen and Campus, located across 922 and 960 Vine Street in Hollywood. Chuck Lorre joined Project Angel Food CEO Richard Ayoub, Trisha Cardoso, president and chief giving officer of The Chuck Lorre Family Foundation, California State Senator Ben Allen, board member Mary Fisher, donors and volunteers for the event.The new building, known as the Community Outreach Center, is intended to complement the expanded kitchen and operations facility that opened on February 5, 2026. While the first building focuses on preparing, storing and distributing meals, the second will provide space for the services and programmes that support clients beyond food delivery. Project Angel Food said the centre will include expanded client and nutrition services, a demonstration kitchen, volunteer facilities, a rooftop herb garden and a Research and Policy Institute. The campus is designed to bring meal production, education, research and direct support together in one location.New kitchen increases meal production capacityThe first building's opening in February marked a significant expansion of Project Angel Food's operations. The new Kitchen and Operations Center more than doubled the organisation's culinary space, increasing it from approximately 7,700 square feet to 16,000 square feet. The upgraded facility also expanded its cooking infrastructure. The kitchen now has three hot cook lines, compared with one previously, along with 90 burners and 21 ovens. These changes are expected to increase annual production capacity from around 1.5 million meals to more than 4.5 million medically tailored meals.The expansion also strengthens storage and distribution. The organisation increased its freezer space and dry storage, while enlarging its packing and distribution areas. This allows it to maintain a frozen meal reserve of up to three weeks, compared with approximately two days previously, helping protect deliveries during emergencies and disruptions. Project Angel Food prepares and delivers approximately 1.5 million medically tailored meals annually to clients across Los Angeles County. Its meals are designed to address the nutritional needs of people dealing with critical and life-threatening illnesses.Outreach centre to focus on nutrition and researchThe Community Outreach Center will extend the organisation's work beyond meal preparation. Expanded client and nutrition services areas will allow staff to assess people's dietary needs, connect them with suitable meals and provide additional support. A demonstration kitchen, called Founders Hall, will offer practical cooking and nutrition education to clients, caregivers, physicians and other organisations working to address food insecurity. The programmes are intended to help people understand how to prepare nutritious meals and, where their health improves, support their transition from receiving fully prepared meals to cooking independently.The building will also include a rooftop herb garden, providing space for community activities and growing fresh ingredients. Its Research and Policy Institute will focus on studying the outcomes of medically tailored meals, sharing findings and building support for wider coverage of such services through programmes including Medi-Cal and Medicare. The organisation's broader aim is to strengthen the role of nutrition in healthcare, particularly for people whose illnesses make access to appropriate food an important part of their treatment and recovery.Chuck Lorre's support helps drive the expansionThe campus is part of Project Angel Food's Rise to the Challenge campaign, a multi-year fundraising effort aimed at increasing the organisation's ability to serve people across Los Angeles County. The Chuck Lorre Family Foundation has been a major supporter of the project, helping make the expansion possible. At the groundbreaking, Lorre spoke about his personal connection to the importance of proper nutrition, saying he had experienced periods without food or healthy food himself. He described being part of an organisation working to address food insecurity as humbling.Project Angel Food CEO Richard Ayoub said the new centre would help the organisation become a national leader in the Food Is Medicine movement. He also announced that approximately $3 million remained to be raised through the campaign to complete the project. The organisation was founded in 1989 during the AIDS crisis and has since delivered more than 20 million meals. With the kitchen already operating and construction now beginning on the Community Outreach Center, the two-building campus is expected to be completed in 2028.
